From Kandariya Mahadeva Temple to Lakshmana Temple and Vishvanatha Temple, the best places to visit in Khajuraho blend iconic landmarks with quiet corners most travelers miss. We have also tucked in genuine hidden gems like Ninora Tal Lake after the headline sights, because the most memorable moments in Khajuraho often happen off the obvious trail. Every entry below is ranked by what real travellers rate most, paired with a vivid photo, the best time to visit, how long to spend, and a direct Google Maps link — so this doubles as a practical travel guide to Khajuraho and a ready-made shortlist for your itinerary. pageContent: Khajuraho ranks among Madhya Pradesh's most rewarding destinations, and it is easy to see why travelers keep returning. Known for carved desire and devotion, unesco-inscribed in stone, it packs a remarkable variety of experiences into one trip. When people search for the best places to visit in Khajuraho, the headline names come up again and again: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple, Lakshmana Temple, Vishvanatha Temple, Khajuraho Western Group (Archaeological Museum), Khajuraho Sound and Light Show (Western Group). Each earns its spot for a reason — together they capture the heritage, spiritual, historical character that defines the region.

Beyond the icons, the must visit places in Khajuraho reward anyone willing to explore a little further. Spots such as Devi Jagadamba Temple, Chitragupta Temple, Parsvanatha Temple (Eastern Group), Adinatha Temple (Eastern Group), Chaturbhuja Temple (Southern Group) round out an itinerary and show a different side of the destination. For the best experience, time your visit thoughtfully: many of the top tourist attractions in Khajuraho are at their finest early in the day or around golden hour, when the light is soft, crowds are thin, and photographs come alive. Most travelers find that two to four unhurried days are enough to cover the essentials without rushing.

Looking for things to do in Khajuraho that go beyond the guidebook? Seek out the quieter finds — Tribal and Folk Art Museum, Khajuraho, Khajuraho Classical Dance Festival, Ninora Tal Lake — where you will trade ticket queues for genuine local atmosphere. This curated guide is built to be the most useful starting point on the internet for your trip: every attraction below includes why it is worth your time, the best time to visit, a realistic duration, and a direct Google Maps search. Use it to shortlist your favourites, then drop them straight into a Trypinn itinerary, invite your crew, and turn a list of must-see places in Khajuraho into a trip that actually happens.

Planning practicalities matter as much as the sights. A typical visit to Khajuraho in Madhya Pradesh works best as a two-to-four-day trip, leaving room to slow down rather than tick boxes. Group the Kandariya Mahadeva Temple and Lakshmana Temple area together to cut travel time, and keep a relaxed half-day spare for the hidden gems and spontaneous detours that make heritage and spiritual and historical so memorable. attractions.name: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple
attractions.description: The tallest and most magnificent of Khajuraho's temples, the Kandariya Mahadeva soars 30.5 metres above its high plinth with a shikhara that replicates the form of Mount Kailash. Its exterior walls bear over 900 sculptural figures in three bands — divine beings, celestial nymphs (apsaras), erotic couples (mithunas), and mythological narratives — carved with extraordinary precision in honey-golden Vindhyan sandstone.
attractions.whyVisit: The apex of Chandela temple art — India's most celebrated medieval sculptural programme on a single temple.

attractions.name: Lakshmana Temple
attractions.description: Dedicated to Vaikuntha Vishnu and completed in 954 CE under Chandela king Dhanga, the Lakshmana Temple is one of the most completely preserved of all Khajuraho's monuments. Set on a massive pancharatha platform with four subsidiary shrines at the corners, its intricately carved exterior depicts processions of elephants, horses, warriors, erotic friezes, and celestial beings across three registers.
attractions.whyVisit: The best-preserved and most harmoniously composed of Khajuraho's Vaishnava temples.

attractions.name: Vishvanatha Temple
attractions.description: Built in 1002 CE, the Vishvanatha Temple is a Shaivite gem in the Western Group featuring a particularly celebrated band of surasundari (beautiful celestial women) sculptures on its exterior — figures writing letters, playing instruments, removing thorns from feet, and bathing in languid, impossibly graceful poses. The original Shivalinga inside is still worshipped daily.
attractions.whyVisit: Khajuraho's finest surasundari sculptures and a living active temple amid tourist monuments.
attractions.bestTime: Morning puja and early light for photography

attractions.name: Khajuraho Western Group (Archaeological Museum)
attractions.description: The Archaeological Survey of India museum adjacent to the Western Group contains sculptures excavated around Khajuraho that are too damaged or small for the temples themselves. Highlights include a damaged but extraordinary sculpture of Vishnu Vaikuntha with lion and boar heads, Chandela-period bronzes, and decorative friezes explaining the symbolic and iconographic programme of the temples.
attractions.whyVisit: Essential context for understanding the symbolism and artistry of Khajuraho's carvings in depth.
attractions.bestTime: Morning, before temple crowds; closed Fridays

attractions.name: Khajuraho Sound and Light Show (Western Group)
attractions.description: A nightly 50-minute open-air spectacular at the Western Group illuminates the temples in changing colours as a dramatic voice narration (in English and Hindi) traces the story of the Chandela dynasty, the temples' construction, and the symbolism of the sculptures. Amitabh Bachchan provides the Hindi narration, lending the show cinematic gravitas.
attractions.whyVisit: The definitive evening introduction to Khajuraho — the temples lit up like jewels with Bachchan's voice booming.
attractions.bestTime: Every evening; October to March for cool comfort

attractions.name: Devi Jagadamba Temple
attractions.description: One of the earliest temples in the Western Group, originally dedicated to Vishnu but later rededicated to Parvati and then Kali. Its sculptures include particularly well-known erotic panels on the south facade and exceptional figures of the river goddesses Ganga and Yamuna on the doorway. The temple's three-part shikhara cluster has weathered beautifully to a warm amber.
attractions.whyVisit: Contains some of the most famous and photographed erotic sculptures in the entire Khajuraho complex.

attractions.name: Chitragupta Temple
attractions.description: The only Khajuraho temple dedicated to Surya (the Sun God), the Chitragupta features a rare image of Surya driving a chariot of seven horses in the central niche of the sanctum, along with processional friezes of eleven-headed Vishnu and exuberant hunting scenes. The temple's relatively modest scale makes it easy to study its sculpture programme in detail.
attractions.whyVisit: Khajuraho's only sun temple and one of the best temples for close-up sculptural study.
attractions.bestTime: Morning — sun illuminates the carvings dramatically from the east

attractions.name: Parsvanatha Temple (Eastern Group)
attractions.description: The largest of Khajuraho's Jain temples, Parsvanatha is also architecturally the finest in the Eastern Group. Though Jain in dedication, it carries almost identical sculptural programmes to the Hindu temples, including sensuous apsaras in characteristic poses (often reproduced in art books) and a celebrated frieze of celestial beauties on its southern face.
attractions.whyVisit: The most sculptural and architecturally impressive of Khajuraho's Jain temples — equal in quality to the Hindu group.

attractions.name: Adinatha Temple (Eastern Group)
attractions.description: A compact but exquisitely carved Jain temple from the 10th century dedicated to the first Jain tirthankara, Adinatha. Three bands of sculptures encircle the exterior with celestial figures, devotees, and scenes of Jain cosmology. The Adinatha image in the sanctum retains its original gem-inset eyes, and the temple sees active Jain pilgrimage.
attractions.whyVisit: A living Jain pilgrimage temple with original gem-set sacred imagery amid the heritage complex.

attractions.name: Chaturbhuja Temple (Southern Group)
attractions.description: The only Khajuraho temple with no erotic sculptures whatsoever, the Chaturbhuja in the Southern Group houses a superb 2.7-metre standing Vishnu image with four arms — one of the finest Chandela sculptures. The temple stands isolated on a hill above Jatkara village, 3 km south of Khajuraho town, and is blissfully uncrowded.
attractions.whyVisit: The exception to the 'erotic temples' narrative — a magnificent isolated temple known mainly to specialists.

attractions.name: Duladeo Temple (Southern Group)
attractions.description: The last great temple built at Khajuraho (early 12th century), Duladeo is dedicated to Shiva and shows the slightly stiffer late Chandela style compared to the flowing 10th-century masterpieces. Its sculptural band is nonetheless rich, and it is the only temple in the Southern Group with a surviving ardhamandapa and mandapa intact.
attractions.whyVisit: A rarely visited late Chandela temple that demonstrates the artistic evolution of the tradition.

attractions.name: Matangeshvara Temple
attractions.description: The only temple at Khajuraho in active daily worship and not under ASI's no-entry archaeological preservation, Matangeshvara is a massive, relatively plain 10th-century Shiva shrine housing a 2.5-metre Shivalinga. During Maha Shivaratri, thousands of pilgrims gather here for an all-night festival that is one of Bundelkhand's most fervent religious gatherings.
attractions.whyVisit: The living, breathing heart of Khajuraho's religious life — still a working temple, not a museum.

attractions.name: Chandela Dynasty History Walk
attractions.description: Local ASI-licensed guides lead context-rich walks through the Western Group explaining the Tantric philosophical symbolism behind the erotic carvings, the 64 yogini cult, the role of kama in Chandela cosmology, and the art historical timeline of the 25 surviving temples from the original 85. The walk transforms a confusing mass of carvings into a coherent spiritual narrative.
attractions.whyVisit: Khajuraho without a guide is like reading a sentence without context — the guided walk reveals the entire meaning.

attractions.name: Ken River Lodge and Ken River
attractions.description: The Ken River flows 24 km from Khajuraho through rocky Vindhyan gorges before entering Panna National Park. The riverside around Khajuraho is excellent for birding — Indian skimmer, river tern, grey-headed fish eagle, and ruddy shelduck are regular. Ken River Lodge, 25 km away at the park's edge, offers jeep safaris for tigers and vulture-watching.
attractions.whyVisit: Pairing tigers and temple sculptures in a single trip — Panna's tigers are among MP's most reliably sighted.
attractions.bestTime: October to June for wildlife; avoid monsoon road flooding

attractions.name: Khajuraho Sculpture Art Market
attractions.description: A cluster of workshops and shops around the Western Group entrance and main market lane where Bundelkhand artisans carve replica Khajuraho figures from local sandstone and soapstone. Watching a craftsman chisel an apsara figure from raw stone is a remarkable spectacle, and the replicas range from mass-produced souvenirs to genuine artisan commissions weeks in the making.
attractions.whyVisit: See the sculptural tradition live — artisans carving Chandela-style figures in real time.

attractions.name: Panna National Park Tiger Safari
attractions.description: Panna National Park, 42 km from Khajuraho, was successfully restocked with tigers after local extinction and now holds a healthy population. Jeep safaris through its rugged Ken River gorge landscape offer sightings of tigers, leopards, wild dogs (dholes), sloth bears, and gharials, as well as 200+ bird species. The park's dramatic ravine scenery is itself exceptional.
attractions.whyVisit: One of MP's most successful tiger conservation stories and a world-class safari 45 minutes from Khajuraho.
attractions.bestTime: February to May (best sightings); October to November

attractions.name: Vishwanath Temple Nandi Sculpture
attractions.description: Opposite the Vishvanatha Temple stands a monolithic Nandi (Shiva's bull) on a separate platform, one of Khajuraho's finest freestanding sculptures. The muscular, serene Nandi gazes toward the Vishvanatha sanctum across an open court, as was customary. The paired composition of Nandi facing the temple shikhara represents one of Khajuraho's most harmonious architectural moments.
attractions.whyVisit: A sculptural and compositional gem often overlooked by visitors rushing between the main temples.

attractions.name: Raneh Falls (Ken Gharial Sanctuary)
attractions.description: The Ken River at Raneh, 22 km from Khajuraho, cascades through a dramatic gorge of naturally occurring crystalline granite columns in hues of pink, red, and grey — the result of ancient volcanic intrusion. The series of waterfalls, pools, and polished rock formations is spectacular, and the gorge edges are part of the Ken Gharial Sanctuary.
attractions.whyVisit: A geologically unique canyon of coloured granite columns with waterfalls — unlike anything else in central India.
attractions.bestTime: August to November (falls running); January to April (gharial basking)

attractions.name: Vamana Temple
attractions.description: Dedicated to Vamana, the dwarf avatar of Vishnu, this elegantly proportioned 11th-century temple in the Eastern Group has a celebrated sculptural programme centred on Vishnu's ten avatars (dashavatara). Its exterior maintains an unusual band of rampant lions alternating with scrollwork at the plinth level, and the overall form is notable for its three-part clustered shikhara.
attractions.whyVisit: Khajuraho's finest Vaishnava iconography outside the Western Group, in a quieter eastern setting.

attractions.name: Local Village Walk — Khajuraho Town
attractions.description: The lanes behind Khajuraho's archaeological zone pass through a living village of Bundeli-speaking communities with whitewashed houses, mud-walled ghee-making dairies, chai stalls beside ancient stepwells, and small fields of mustard and wheat. Walking this neighbourhood at dawn reveals the agricultural rhythms of Bundelkhand entirely unchanged by temple tourism.
attractions.whyVisit: Step 300 metres behind the monuments and find a completely untouched village India — a reality check and delight.

attractions.name: Bijamandal Excavated Temple Site
attractions.description: An ongoing ASI excavation site near the Eastern Group that is gradually uncovering the foundations and scattered sculpture fragments of an 11th-century temple complex — the lost Bijamandal — buried under centuries of earth. The exposed foundations, carved blocks, and in-situ sculptures give a rare and dramatic sense of an archaeological discovery in progress.
attractions.whyVisit: Archaeology live — a temple being unearthed in real time, invisible to most tourists passing by.
attractions.bestTime: Weekday mornings when excavation may be active

attractions.name: Ghantai Temple (Eastern Group)
attractions.description: Only the pillared entrance hall (mandapa) of the 11th-century Ghantai temple survives, but it is extraordinarily beautiful — slender stone columns rising to bracket capitals carved with chains of bells (ghanta), erotic panels, and celestial figures, all open to the sky. The Jain temple's remaining pillars stand among mature trees, creating one of Khajuraho's most poetic ruined spaces.
attractions.whyVisit: Khajuraho's most romantic ruin — a skeletal colonnade of bell-carved pillars open to the Madhya Pradesh sky.

attractions.name: Tribal and Folk Art Museum, Khajuraho
attractions.description: A small but impressive museum in Khajuraho town dedicated to the tribal and folk arts of Madhya Pradesh's Bundelkhand and Vindhya regions, housing Gond paintings, Baiga tattooing artefacts, iron Gondi deity figures (lauha devta), terracotta votive objects, and traditional textiles. It offers a counterpoint to the high Chandela courtly art of the temples.
attractions.whyVisit: The visual culture of Bundelkhand's tribes — an artistic world as rich as the temples, almost entirely unknown.

attractions.name: Khajuraho Classical Dance Festival
attractions.description: Held annually in late February or early March against the floodlit backdrop of the Western Group temples, the Khajuraho Dance Festival is a week-long celebration of Indian classical dance forms. Bharatanatyam, Odissi, Kathak, Manipuri, and Kuchipudi performances are staged outdoors each evening, their fluid sculptural forms mirroring the stone dancers carved on the walls behind them.
attractions.whyVisit: Classical dance performed before the temples that inspired it — one of India's most visually perfect cultural events.
attractions.bestTime: Late February to early March (festival week)

attractions.name: Ninora Tal Lake
attractions.description: A peaceful seasonal lake 3 km from Khajuraho town, surrounded by scrub forest and agricultural land, that attracts migratory waterfowl from November to February including bar-headed geese, painted storks, grey herons, and various ducks. Largely unknown to tourists, it is a favourite of local birders and offers a quiet natural escape from the temple circuit.
attractions.whyVisit: Khajuraho's secret birdwatching lake — extraordinary winter wildfowl, zero tourism infrastructure.
